title: xor a (xor a b) = b
statement: For every natural a, b: xor(a, xor(a, b)) equals b.

formal.statement: ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.xor x0 (AxNat.xor x0 x1)) x1))

evidence.supports: Nat.xor_xor_cancel_left is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- xor_xor_cancel_left 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.xor_xor_cancel_left[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count (expected >= 1) decides the exit status, never `grep -q` under pipefail. Anchored with `[[:space:]]`, never a literal tab, per this ledger's own grep-dialect gotcha. `--release` is mandatory: this tool builds `creal`/`complex`/`cpoint`, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: At the discriminating concrete pair (a, b) = (3, 5), xor(3, xor(3, 5)) def-eq's to 5 (xor(3,5)=6, xor(3,6)=5), and the theorem's conclusion does NOT def-eq to the negative control 4; and the theorem re-derives against a genuinely free (a, b) pair, not merely a concrete instance.
evidence.notes: A concrete instantiation alone can hide a defect a symbolic build exposes (and vice versa), so both are checked. (3, 5) is chosen because xor(3,5)=6 is neither operand, giving the negative control (4) something to discriminate against. This single test also covers F:nat-xor-xor-cancel-right's compute evidence (same fixture, same discriminating pair).

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*).

No `ml430` fact for this exact statement was found in the ledger. Read directly at the pinned commit `c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f`, `Mathlib/Data/Nat/Bitwise.lean` cites `Nat.xor_assoc`/`Nat.xor_xor_cancel_left`/`Nat.xor_xor_cancel_right`/`Nat.xor_ne_zero_iff` in `xor_trichotomy`'s proof but does not define them there -- they are Lean4 core lemmas about `Nat.xor`/`^^^`, not Mathlib-authored, so no `ml430` mirror fact exists to flip; this lands as a new local fact instead (see F:nat-xor-assoc's notes, which record the same check in more detail).

Third of the four sub-targets Mathlib's own `xor_trichotomy` proof composes toward `F:ml430-nat-lt-xor-cases-c43a1e85` (`xor_assoc`, `xor_xor_cancel_left`, `xor_xor_cancel_right`, `xor_ne_zero_iff`); `xor_ne_zero_iff` is NOT built by this fact.

A GENUINE COMPLICATION this fact's route hits that `F:nat-xor-assoc` did not: the natural per-bit cancel identity `xor_bit x (xor_bit x y) = y` is FALSE for a general `y : Nat` -- only for `y in {0, 1}` (confirmed by a Python truth-table simulation before any Rust was written: `xor_bit(3, xor_bit(3, 5)) = 0 != 5`). `xor_assoc`'s per-bit identity stayed at the `digitize`/`Bool` level throughout and never needed this restriction; this one's conclusion is a bare `y`, forcing a match back to the raw operand. The fix is a new `y <= 1` round-trip lemma (`round_trip_le_one` in `xor_algebra.rs`): given `Le y 1`, `Nat.le_succ_succ` lifts it to `Lt y 2` (`succ (num 1)` is `refl`-defeq to `num 2`, so no separate lemma is needed for the bound), then `Nat.lt_two_cases` splits into `y = 0`/`y = 1` via `Or.elim` (the kernel's `Or.elim : (a b c : Prop) -> Or a b -> (a -> c) -> (b -> c) -> c`, not a new combinator), each branch closed by transporting the hypothesis along the equality and a `refl` at the computed literal -- the same "build refl of one side, let defeq do the rest" device `beq_digitize_one` uses. `Nat.testBit` is always in `{0, 1}` (`Nat.testBit_le_one`), which is exactly what makes the per-bit application of this lemma legal inside `declare_xor_xor_cancel_left`.

The full per-bit route: `xor_bit_cancel_left(x, y, h_le_y) : Eq (xor_bit x (xor_bit x y)) y` lifts a NEW `Bool`-level self-cancel lemma (`bool_xor_self_cancel_left : Eq (xor_fn a (xor_fn a b)) b`, proved by a 2-level `Bool.rec` split -- `a = false` closes by `refl` for any `b`; `a = true` needs one more split on `b`, both leaves closing by `refl` directly, no third level unlike `xor_assoc`'s `bool_xor_assoc`) through the same digitize/round-trip machinery `xor_bit_assoc` uses, landing on `y` itself via `round_trip_le_one`. `Nat.xor_xor_cancel_left` then applies `Nat.testBit_xor` to reduce `testBit (xor a (xor a b)) i` to `xor_bit (testBit a i) (xor_bit (testBit a i) (testBit b i))`, applies `xor_bit_cancel_left` at `(testBit a i, testBit b i)` with `Nat.testBit_le_one` supplying the bound, and closes with `Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq`.

A genuine bug found and fixed via a throwaway `#[cfg(test)]` bisecting probe (calling `round_trip_le_one`/`bool_xor_self_cancel_left`/`xor_bit_cancel_left`/`declare_xor_xor_cancel_left` directly against a prelude built with the two new `declare_*` calls temporarily disabled, per the standing rule that reading a poisoned whole-suite `TypeMismatch` is slower than isolating the defect): the per-bit chain in `declare_xor_xor_cancel_left` mislabeled an intermediate, substituting `testBit(xor a b, i)`'s value directly as the chain's target rather than substituting it INTO the outer `xor_bit(testBit a i, _)` combine first -- i.e. confusing `xor_bit(tb_a, tb_b)` (the substituted value) with `xor_bit(tb_a, xor_bit(tb_a, tb_b))` (the actually-needed cascaded expression matching `xor_bit_cancel_left`'s own LHS shape). All three helper functions type-checked correctly in isolation via the probe; the defect was purely in the theorem-level wiring, found in one probe-and-fix cycle rather than by reading the ~150-test poisoned failure list. The probe module was removed before this fact was recorded.
